newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to step up investment in central America.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to step up investment in central America.

text.p: Taiwan, under constant diplomatic pressure by rival China, said on Saturday it would step up trade and investment Central America to boost relations with its allies.
"We hope to develop steady relations with our central American allies and open a new page of reciprocal international cooperation," a statement issued by the Presidential Office said.
Most of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies are underdeveloped states in Africa and central America.
The island's top economic policymaking body would set up a special task force to promote trade and investment with Central America, the Presidential Office said without elaboration.

Taiwan and China split after a civil war in 1949. Beijing considers Taiwan a renegade province and seeks to isolate the island completely from international arenas until it can be reunified under mainland sovereignty.

Top Taiwan officials have planned four foreign damage-control missions since Taipei's largest ally, South Africa, shocked the island in November by announcing it would switch ties to Beijing by the end of 1997.
Foreign Minister John Chang is due leave for Guatemala for the December 29 signing of a peace pact between the Guatemalan government and leftist rebels.
Chang visited South Africa in December in a failed attempt to rescue ties and will return to Pretoria in January along with visits to several neigbouring African countries.
Vice-President Lien Chan is scheduled to visit Nicaragua, a Taipei ally, in January for the inauguration of President-elect Arnoldo Aleman.
